text: dsh-yunoseek-skin 是面向 DSH Web GUI 的 Yunoseek 视觉与提示词插件。它通过客户端 theme token 覆盖层统一调整浅色和深色配色，并注入聊天助手头像及 Hero 光晕样式；非 official 构建还可注册侧栏和欢迎区品牌标记。节点端默认向全局 system prompt 注册 Yunoseek 身份文本，顺序早于 harness 身份提示词，也可在 profile 配置中关闭或替换。适合希望为 DSH 网页界面换用粉色 Yunoseek 风格并加载对应助手人设的用户；不需要额外 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-yunoseek-skin gives the DSH web GUI a pink Yunoseek theme, assistant avatar and Hero styling. It registers a Yunoseek identity section before the harness prompt; profile configuration can disable or replace it. No extra API key or external service is needed.
想把 DSH 网页界面换成粉色主题。
有没有能给 DSH 聊天助手换头像和欢迎页风格的插件？
让 DSH 的浅色和深色界面都使用一套粉色配色。
我想让 DSH 默认用 Yunoseek 的身份提示词。
I want a pink Yunoseek theme for the DSH web interface.
Can DSH prepend a custom persona prompt to every conversation?
dsh-yunoseek-skin 的功能「粉色主题」：客户端注册 theme token 覆盖层，为浅色和深色模式分别设置粉色品牌色、背景与界面语义色。插件加载后自动应用。
dsh-yunoseek-skin 的功能「身份提示词」：节点端在 systemPrompt 服务就绪后注册 Yunoseek 身份 section，默认使用内嵌文本并排在 harness 身份之前；profile 配置可关闭或替换文本。
dsh-yunoseek-skin 的功能「聊天视觉样式」：客户端挂载样式表，为助手聊天行显示头像并调整 Hero 光晕；非 official 构建还注册侧栏和 Hero 品牌标记。
我想给 DSH 的聊天回复加上固定的助手头像。
I want every DSH agent to start with a Yunoseek identity prompt.

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · dsh-yunoseek-skin：Yunoseek pink skin for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) web GUI. It restyles the DSH browser UI with the pink art direction of the yunoseek chat UI (`#E91E8C` / `#FF6B9D` gradients, pink tints) while reusing every DSH layout and component unchanged, through the standard client-plugin interfaces:

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · dsh-yunoseek-skin：- **Pink token layer** — a theme `overrideTokens` layer over the `--dsw-*` semantic tokens and the `--dsw-static-deepseek-*` scale, every token carrying explicit light and dark values from yunoseek's two palettes. The skin is always on and follows the user's light/dark/system preference; no settings change needed.
- **Art direction sheet** — the pink Hero glow recolor per palette, and the **assistant avatar** painted into every chat assistant row via its stable `data-chat-flow-kind` attribute (the host's CSS Modules class names are hashed and not addressable cross-package).
- **Brand marks** (non-`official` builds only) — the yunoseek logo in the sidebar brand row, the gradient "Yunoseek" wordmark, and the welcome artwork in the conversation Hero seat. Official DeepSeek Harness compositions already own those single-occupant slots with the built-in brand, so the skin yields them by default (see "Build profile" below).
- **Yunoseek identity prompt** — the node half registers the yunoseek system prompt (`assets/system-prompt.js`) as the first system-prompt section, so every assembled system prompt starts with the Yunoseek persona.
dsh-yunoseek-skin README · dsh-yunoseek-skin：extra system prompt takes ~1200 tokens and can be banned/started though the method written in release 0.2.0

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Yunoseek identity prompt：Beyond the visuals, the plugin injects the yunoseek identity prompt into the model. Its node half registers a `systemPrompt` section named `yunoseek:identity` with order `-200`, which renders **before** the harness identity (`-100`) and the deployment persona (`0`) — the very first text the model reads for every turn. The default text is the yunoseek system prompt from `assets/system-prompt.js`, embedded at build time.

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Yunoseek identity prompt：The injection is on by default and applies globally to every agent in the profile (the section lives in the prompt registry's global layer). To disable it or replace the text, override the row from your profile patch (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`) — a later layer that replaces the row's `config` value:

```yaml
- update:
    - id: yunoseek-skin
      config:
        enabled: false        # skin only, no prompt injection

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Yunoseek identity prompt：```yaml
- update:
    - id: yunoseek-skin
      config:
        prompt: |

Config is read at boot, so restart `dsh web` after changing it. The section text is static: it carries no `{{variable}}` references — a custom prompt containing `{{…}}` fails prompt assembly on purpose (fail loud keeps a malformed prompt out of the model request).
**modified prompt takes about 1200 extra tokens**
dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Install：Requirements: a dsh installation (the `dsh` CLI) and a web profile — the default GUI profile is named `web`.

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · From GitHub：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:<owner>/dsh-yunoseek-skin
```

A git install fetches sources, not built artifacts, so pnpm runs the package's `prepare` script to build `lib/`. pnpm ≥ 10 refuses to run a git dependency's `prepare` until explicitly allowed — the first `add` fails and dsh prints the exact package key; copy it into the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  dsh-yunoseek-skin: true
```

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · From GitHub：then re-run the `add`. (That allowance is permission to execute the package's code at install time; only allow packages whose source you trust, and pin a commit: `github:<owner>/dsh-yunoseek-skin#<sha>`.) Then (re)start your `dsh web` once so the new roster row composes; later code changes to the skin hot-reload through the web HMR chain.

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · From npm or a tarball：Prebuilt options need no build allowance:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-yunoseek-skin        # npm, lib/ built at publish time
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-yunoseek-skin-0.2.0.tgz   # pnpm pack
```

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-yunoseek-skin
```

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Build profile and the brand seats：The tsdown config pins `DSH_CLIENT_BUILD_PROFILE` (default `official`). In an `official` build the skin applies the token layer, avatar sheet, and Hero glow **only** — official web compositions contain the built-in deepseek brand, which owns the `sidebar.brand.mark` / `sidebar.brand.name` / `conversation.hero.brand.mark` seats and must not collide. To show the yunoseek marks instead (e.g. a dev/self-built web, or after disabling the built-in brand row), build with:

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Build profile and the brand seats：```sh
DSH_CLIENT_BUILD_PROFILE=dev pnpm install   # rebuilds lib/ with brand marks on
```

and, when your composition still carries the built-in brand row, disable it in the profile patch (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- update:
    - id: ui-brand-official
      disabled: true
```
section: Build profile and the brand seats

text:
dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Build：```sh
pnpm install    # installs tsdown and runs prepare, emitting lib/
```

The `prepare` script is self-contained (docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md): it builds from `src/` with a dedicated tsdown config — no monorepo context, no project references, no typechecking. Outputs: `lib/index.js` (ESM node half) and `lib/client.js` (CJS browser half).

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Distribution：This is a standard dsh bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` (patch `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the `yunoseek-skin` row) and `dsh.client` (`platform: "web"`, informational `inject` edges). To publish: create a repository under your GitHub account, push this directory, and users install with `dsh plugin --profile web add github:<owner>/dsh-yunoseek-skin`; or `npm publish` with `lib/` built, or ship `pnpm pack` tarballs.

dsh-yunoseek-skin README · Known limitations：- The identity prompt is global and forward-most: a later layer that registers a `complete: true` system-prompt section replaces the whole prompt for an agent, and the injected text disappears there (the registry's documented complete-section behavior).
- Custom prompt text must not contain `{{…}}` — prompt variables render strictly and an unknown reference fails assembly.
- The assistant avatar is painted into chat rows by selector: `[data-chat-flow-kind="assistant-step"]::before` with a fixed 34px geometry. If ui-conversation changes that attribute or row geometry, the rule (in `src/client/styles.ts`) needs a revisit.
- The sidebar and Hero marks are skipped in `official` builds by design (single-occupant brand slots); see above for the dev-profile path.
- The Hero glow rule targets `[data-phase="hero"] svg ellipse`; a future Hero redesign may move the glow out of an SVG ellipse.
